problem_signature: RH / exact zeta zero-location / analytic-number-theory child: zero-density-to-exclusion threshold inside prime/explicit-formula uniform-tail search

root_binding.statement: Every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s) satisfies Re(rho)=1/2.

object_context: Audit whether currently proved zero-density and zero-free estimates, optionally combined with rigorous finite-height zero verification, can furnish the genuinely uniform tail/exclusion mechanism demanded by RH-ANA-003. The immediate quantity is N(sigma,T), the number of nontrivial zeros with Re(rho)>=sigma and |Im(rho)|<=T. The decision question is not whether density improves, but whether the available bound can be converted without circularity into zero occupancy for every fixed sigma>1/2.
quantity_of_interest: For each fixed sigma>1/2, an unconditional certificate that N(sigma,T)=0 for all T, or an equivalent local-tail certificate that excludes every off-critical zero.

scope.height: all heights; finite verified prefix may calibrate only
scope.authority_boundary: experience and analogy guide search only; numerics calibrate/falsify only

fibre_contents_consulted: current RAKL 3.0.0 core workflow, v3 experience substrate, metrology, pre-action receipt and method_specs.py

current_primary_sources.citation: Larry Guth and James Maynard, New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, Annals of Mathematics 203 (2026), 623-675.
current_primary_sources.key_claim: N(sigma,T) <= T^(30(1-sigma)/13+o(1)) after combining their theorem with Ingham in the stated ranges.

current_primary_sources.citation: Chiara Bellotti, An explicit log-free zero density estimate for the Riemann zeta-function, arXiv:2405.12545.
current_primary_sources.key_claim: Bounds of form N(sigma,T) <= C T^(B(1-sigma)); for one displayed uniform regime sigma>=0.9927, B=1.448 and C=1.62e11 over 3e12<T<=exp(6.7e12).

current_primary_sources.citation: Michael J. Mossinghoff, Timothy S. Trudgian, Andrew Yang, Explicit zero-free regions for the Riemann zeta-function, arXiv:2212.06867.
current_primary_sources.key_claim: No zeros in an explicit Vinogradov-Korobov type region adjacent to sigma=1.

current_primary_sources.citation: Dave Platt and Tim Trudgian, The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3·10^12, Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 53 (2021), 792-797; arXiv:2004.09765.
current_primary_sources.key_claim: All zeros with 0<gamma<=3e12 lie on the critical line.

equivalent_formulations: For every fixed sigma>1/2 and every T>0, N(sigma,T)=0.
Finite verified height H plus, for every sigma>1/2 and every dyadic T>=H, the local tail count N(sigma,2T)-N(sigma,T)=0.
near_solved_analogues: Rigorous finite-height verification gives exact zero occupancy only on a bounded height interval.
Explicit zero-free regions give exact occupancy zero only in a shrinking region adjacent to Re(s)=1.
Zero-density theorems give global cardinality upper bounds on off-line zeros but not occupancy zero.
Even the Density Hypothesis N(sigma,T)<<T^(2(1-sigma)+epsilon) is explicitly described in primary literature as weaker than RH.

method_transfers.transfer: turn a counting upper bound into emptiness only after the upper bound for the relevant local count is strictly below 1
required_assumptions: bound applies to the exact target region
all constants and ranges are explicit if a numerical <1 test is used
disanalogies: global cumulative N(sigma,T) is nondecreasing and can retain old zeros; a bounded positive global count does not remove them
asymptotic T^a bounds with a>0 grow and cannot cross the <1 threshold for large T

method_transfers.transfer: pair an exact finite prefix with a theorem excluding every later dyadic block
required_assumptions: finite verification is rigorous and exhaustive through H
tail theorem covers every block above H
disanalogies: a density estimate controlling only total count or average proportion is not a blockwise zero theorem
numerical height cannot substitute for an infinite tail theorem

structural_analogy.name: rare-defect rate versus zero-defect certificate
structural_analogy.difference_witness: analytic zero counts have symmetry, zero-free subregions and cumulative height structure not present in generic reliability models

hostile_controls: A hypothetical zeta-like count with exactly one off-critical zero above the finite verification height is compatible with every upper bound whose right side is >=1 at that height.
A uniform O(1) global density bound with constant >=1 would still permit finitely many off-critical zeros and therefore would not imply RH.
A density-proportion tending to zero can coexist with infinitely many sparse off-critical zeros.

forbidden_shortcuts: zero-free region silently extended to the full half-strip
RH-equivalent assumption used as remainder control
